contentBlocks.title: A. REPORT ON FREE ACCESS TO EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES THROUGH THE UNIVERSITY LIBRARY WEBSITE

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University) promotes inclusive access to knowledge and educational resources through its well-established Library and Information Centre. In addition to catering to the academic and research requirements of its students and faculty members, the University makes a wide range of educational resources accessible to the general public through its official Library website.

The online library portal serves as an open gateway to diverse academic and informational resources, enabling students, researchers, academicians and members of the public to access educational materials free of cost. This initiative extends the University's knowledge-sharing commitment beyond its campus and supports independent learning, academic exploration and lifelong learning.

contentBlocks.title: Institutional Library Resources & Public Digital Gateway
rows: Digital resource-platform links listed on the Library website

contentBlocks.text: The University maintains an extensive library collection comprising more than 1,75,000 resources, including books, reference materials, journals, magazines, newspapers, research publications and digital resources.

In addition to the physical library collection, the University provides access to numerous online educational platforms through its website, extending the availability of academic information beyond the University's physical premises.

contentBlocks.title: 2. Free Access to Digital Educational Resources

contentBlocks.text: The University's Library website provides direct links to a wide range of digital educational resources covering different academic disciplines and areas of general interest. These resources are accessible through the website and enable users to explore educational content without necessarily requiring institutional membership or paid subscriptions.

These platforms offer access to academic publications, electronic books, research articles, newspapers, magazines, dissertations and knowledge resources. The availability of these links through the University's public website enables individuals beyond the University community to benefit from the educational resources.

A significant feature of the University's digital library initiative is the provision of links to internationally recognised open-access educational platforms. These platforms make scholarly publications, research materials and educational content freely available to students, researchers, academicians and the general public.

Through these platforms, users can access a wide spectrum of academic materials without being restricted to the University's student or faculty community. This facilitates wider dissemination of knowledge and encourages research-based learning among the public.

contentBlocks.title: 4. Access to Institutional and Scholarly Databases

contentBlocks.text: The University Library website also provides information and links to reputed national and international academic databases and electronic information resources, including EBSCO, Springer, JSTOR, ProQuest, J-Gate, N-List and Scopus, among others.

These platforms offer access to scholarly journals, research articles, books and other academic publications. While certain resources are available through open-access arrangements, others operate through institutional subscriptions and may have specific access conditions, including institutional network or authorised user requirements.
The availability of these resources through the library portal provides a centralised point of reference for users seeking quality academic and research information.

contentBlocks.title: 5. Additional Digital Learning and Information Resources

contentBlocks.text: Apart from academic books and journals, the University Library website provides links to several other educational and informational resources, including:

contentBlocks.title: Categories of Extended E-Resources
paragraphs: • E-newspapers: Access to leading newspapers such as The Hindu, Deccan Herald, Times of India, Deccan Chronicle and Economic Times.
• E-magazines: Access to publications such as India Today, Business Today, Outlook, Digit and Reader's Digest.
• General Knowledge and Current Affairs: Educational resources supporting awareness of national and international developments.
• Research Repositories: Access to dissertations, theses and scholarly research publications.
• Digital Book Collections: Access to electronic books covering diverse subjects and areas of knowledge.

contentBlocks.text: These resources are useful not only for university students but also for competitive examination aspirants, independent learners, researchers and members of the general public.

Conclusion: Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University) demonstrates its commitment to knowledge dissemination and inclusive education by providing an extensive range of digital educational resources through its publicly accessible Library website. With 42 listed digital resource-platform links across different categories, alongside access to numerous open educational repositories and scholarly information platforms, the University creates opportunities for individuals to access quality educational materials beyond the boundaries of its campus. By facilitating access to open-access books, journals, research publications, dissertations, newspapers, magazines and other educational resources, the University extends the benefits of its academic infrastructure to the wider community. This initiative reflects its commitment to democratization of knowledge, digital inclusion, research promotion and lifelong learning.

B. REPORT ON OPEN ACCESS EDUCATIONAL CONTENT MADE AVAILABLE TO THE GENERAL PUBLIC

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti University has undertaken a distinctive and commendable initiative by making a substantial collection of faculty-developed educational resources freely accessible to the general public through digital platforms. This initiative reflects the University's progressive vision of democratizing education, promoting knowledge sharing and extending the benefits of higher education beyond the conventional boundaries of the campus.

While digital learning resources are increasingly being adopted by higher education institutions, a structured initiative to make faculty-created academic content openly available to society represents a significant and distinctive institutional commitment. Such initiatives are practiced by relatively few universities in a sustained and comprehensive manner. Kristu Jayanti University's effort therefore stands out as an exemplary practice that reinforces its commitment to inclusive education, academic outreach and social responsibility.

The University has made 156 educational video resources available through online platforms, particularly YouTube. These videos cover a wide range of academic disciplines, enabling learners from diverse educational backgrounds to access subject-specific knowledge without any geographical or institutional restrictions.

contentBlocks.title: Disciplines Covered by Video Lectures
paragraphs: The video resources encompass subjects and topics from:
• Accounting and Finance
• Economics and Commerce
• Management and Professional Management Studies
• Psychology and Social Sciences
• Forensic Science
• Life Sciences
• English, Kannada and Hindi
• Media Studies

contentBlocks.text: The content includes lectures and learning materials on financial analytics, accounting, taxation, GST, banking, entrepreneurship, economic concepts, forensic science, scientific principles, communication, literature and media-related subjects. This multidisciplinary coverage makes the resources valuable to students, researchers, educators, competitive examination aspirants and lifelong learners.

In addition to video lectures, the University has facilitated access to 63 other digital educational resources through various online platforms. These resources include presentations, academic materials, subject-specific learning content, interactive exercises and other knowledge-sharing resources.

These digital materials complement the video-based resources by offering varied formats of learning, encouraging independent study, reinforcing conceptual understanding and supporting self-paced learning.

A significant feature of this initiative is that access to these educational resources is not confined to the students or faculty of Kristu Jayanti University. The resources are made available online for the benefit of the general public, irrespective of institutional affiliation.

This open-access approach reflects the University's commitment to ensuring that quality academic knowledge reaches a wider audience. Students from other institutions, teachers, research scholars, professionals and members of the public can benefit from these resources without being required to enroll in a university program.

By leveraging digital platforms, the University has transformed faculty expertise into a wider public learning resource. This initiative strengthens the University's role not merely as a center for formal education but also as a proactive contributor to community learning, educational inclusion and the wider dissemination of knowledge.

Kristu Jayanti University's initiative of providing free and open access to 219 educational resources, comprising 156 video resources and 63 other digital learning materials, is a noteworthy institutional practice that deserves special recognition. The initiative goes beyond conventional teaching and learning practices by extending the University's academic contributions to the wider community. It demonstrates a forward-looking approach to educational outreach, where knowledge created within the institution is shared for the benefit of society at large.

This distinctive initiative exemplifies the University's commitment to the philosophy that education and knowledge should transcend institutional boundaries and remain accessible to all. By making faculty-generated academic content freely available to the public, Kristu Jayanti University demonstrates an exemplary model of inclusive, technology-enabled and socially responsible higher education.

contentBlocks.title: 1. CERTIFICATE COURSE ON SPORTS NUTRITION
paragraphs: Duration: 1 September – 30 October 2025

Objective: To provide participants with fundamental knowledge of sports nutrition, dietary requirements, nutritional planning and the role of balanced nutrition in enhancing physical performance, fitness and overall well-being.

Write-up on the Programme: The Centre for Physical Education and Fitness, in collaboration with the Department of Life Sciences, organized a Certificate Course on Sports Nutrition from 1 September to 30 October 2025. The programme focused on the significance of nutrition in sports performance, physical fitness and health management. It aimed to equip participants with an understanding of essential nutrients, dietary planning, hydration, energy requirements and nutritional strategies for physical activities. The course provided valuable insights into the relationship between nutrition and athletic performance, encouraging participants to adopt informed dietary practices for improved fitness and well-being. Certificates of completion were awarded to successful participants.

contentBlocks.title: 2. CERTIFICATE COURSE ON COMPETENCY MAPPING
paragraphs: Duration: 8 – 26 September 2025

Objective: To develop an understanding of competency mapping and its application in identifying, assessing and developing individual competencies for improved personal, academic and professional effectiveness.

Write-up on the Programme: The Department of Psychology, School of Humanities and Social Sciences, organized a Certificate Course on Competency Mapping from 8 to 26 September 2025. The programme focused on introducing participants to the concept, significance and practical applications of competency mapping. It provided insights into identifying individual strengths, assessing behavioural and professional competencies, and understanding the role of competency-based approaches in personal and career development. The course also highlighted the importance of aligning individual capabilities with organizational and professional expectations. The programme enabled participants to gain a better understanding of competency assessment and its relevance in enhancing individual effectiveness and employability. Certificates of completion were awarded to the participants.

contentBlocks.title: 3. CERTIFICATE COURSE ON VOICES FROM THE MARGINS: EXPLORING INDIGENOUS (DALIT AND TRIBAL) NARRATIVES
paragraphs: Duration: 15 September – 18 October 2025

Objective: To introduce participants to indigenous, Dalit and tribal narratives and develop an understanding of marginalized voices, cultural identities, social realities and literary representations through critical engagement with diverse texts and perspectives.

Write-up on the Programme: The Department of English, School of Humanities and Social Sciences, organized a 30-hour Certificate Course titled Voices from the Margins: Exploring Indigenous (Dalit and Tribal) Narratives from 15 September to 18 October 2025. The programme aimed to create awareness of marginalized literary traditions, indigenous identities and socio-cultural experiences through critical engagement with Dalit and tribal narratives. The course explored themes of social justice, identity, representation, cultural heritage and inclusion. As part of the programme, an expert session on Dalit Poetry was delivered by Dr. Abhisarika Prajapati, Associate Professor and Head, Department of English, REVA University, Bengaluru, on 19 September 2025. The programme provided participants with an opportunity to engage with diverse literary perspectives and develop a deeper understanding of the experiences and contributions of marginalized communities. Certificates of completion and appreciation were awarded to the respective participants and resource person.

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti University, through its various centers and cells, organized several programs and initiatives on campus during the academic year 2025–2026. These activities focused on community service, women's empowerment, social inclusion, health awareness and inclusive communication. The programs provided opportunities for students, volunteers and other participants to engage in socially meaningful activities and contribute to community welfare.

contentBlocks.title: COMPUTER LITERACY PROGRAMME FOR SLUM AND MIGRANT CHILDREN (12 September 2025)
paragraphs: On 12 September 2025, JES conducted a computer literacy program for children from slum and migrant communities. The program aimed to improve digital awareness and introduce basic computer skills among underprivileged children. A total of 28 students participated in the initiative and received an opportunity to develop basic computer knowledge and familiarity with technology. The program focused on promoting digital inclusion and providing children with essential technological skills to support their educational development.

contentBlocks.title: SRUJANA – ART, CRAFT AND FOOD STALL (26 August 2025)
paragraphs: On 26 August 2025, the Women Empowerment Cell organized an art, craft and food stall under the SRUJANA initiative on the university campus. The program aimed to encourage creativity, develop entrepreneurial skills and provide a platform for showcasing products created by participants. The stall featured a variety of art and craft items alongside food products, highlighting the creative abilities and practical skills of the individuals involved. A total of 22 center volunteers actively contributed to organizing and managing the stalls, while the program recorded a reach of 130 participants. The initiative provided an opportunity for visitors to explore the displayed products, interact with the volunteers and appreciate their creativity and efforts. It also promoted awareness of small-scale entrepreneurial activities and the importance of supporting creative skills and self-employment opportunities. Through this initiative, the Women Empowerment Cell encouraged community participation, skill development and the recognition of individual talents.

contentBlocks.title: SRUJANA – ART, CRAFT AND FOOD STALL (24 October 2025)
paragraphs: On 24 October 2025, the Women Empowerment Cell organized another edition of the SRUJANA art, craft and food stall on the university campus. The initiative aimed to promote creativity, encourage entrepreneurial thinking and provide opportunities for showcasing artistic talents and practical skills. The event featured a range of handmade craft products, creative art pieces and food items, offering participants a platform to display their work and engage with the university community. A total of 76 center volunteers actively contributed to the planning, coordination and management of the stalls, ensuring the smooth conduct of the program. The event recorded a reach of 190 participants, who visited the stalls, explored the products and interacted with the volunteers. The initiative encouraged women to recognize their creative abilities, gain exposure to entrepreneurial activities and develop confidence in presenting and promoting their products. Through SRUJANA, the Women Empowerment Cell continued its efforts to support creative expression, community engagement, skill development and women's empowerment.

contentBlocks.title: CAMPUSPRENEURS (23 September 2025)
paragraphs: The Department of Management, School of Business and Management, Kristu Jayanti University, organized Campuspreneurs 2025, a stall-based entrepreneurial exhibition, on 23 September 2025 for III BBA students. The event aimed to provide hands-on entrepreneurial exposure and develop creativity, innovation, teamwork and customer interaction skills among students. A total of 16 exhibits involving 96 student participants were showcased, attracting approximately 400 visitors to the exhibition hall.

The stalls featured a variety of business concepts, including eco-friendly products, sustainable lifestyle items, herbal and organic personal care products, handmade décor, books, games, fashion accessories and food products. Students actively participated in planning, setting up and promoting their stalls while interacting with visitors and explaining their products and business ideas. The exhibition provided practical exposure to entrepreneurial decision-making, pricing, marketing, sales and consumer behavior. The activity enhanced students' confidence, leadership, communication and teamwork skills while enabling them to apply classroom concepts in a real-world setting. Overall, Campuspreneurs 2025 served as an experiential learning platform that encouraged entrepreneurial thinking and strengthened students' practical business skills.

contentBlocks.title: CAMPUS FARMERS’ MARKET 2025 (29 August 2025)
paragraphs: The Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC) of Kristu Jayanti University organized the Campus Farmers’ Market – Vegetable and Fruits Mela on 29 August 2025 as part of the Viksit Bharat @ 2047 initiative. The program aimed to promote direct engagement between farmers and consumers, encourage community-based agricultural enterprise and support local products under the Government of India’s One District One Product (ODOP) initiative.

The market featured Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) from Chitradurga, Vijayapura and Chintamani, along with Greenkraft Producer Company Limited, showcasing fresh agricultural produce. By sourcing products directly from farmers, the initiative sought to ensure better returns for producers, eliminate intermediaries and provide consumers with access to fresh and organic produce. The event also featured stalls offering local snacks, flowers and handmade products, providing visibility to local producers and small-scale enterprises. Organized in collaboration with the Women’s Empowerment Cell, the initiative promoted local entrepreneurship and community participation. Overall, the Campus Farmers’ Market strengthened the connection between farmers and consumers while supporting sustainable agricultural practices, rural livelihoods and local economic development.

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti University is committed to promoting lifelong learning through vocational training, skill development and capacity-building initiatives. The University organises structured programmes and learning activities to enhance knowledge, develop professional and leadership competencies, and strengthen institutional effectiveness. These initiatives provide opportunities for continuous learning, knowledge sharing and practical exposure to diverse areas of personal, professional and organisational development. The activities documented in this annexure reflect the University's commitment to extending learning opportunities beyond the campus and fostering a culture of lifelong learning and community engagement.

contentBlocks.title: PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME ON EMPOWERING INSTITUTIONS FOR SUSTAINABLE EXCELLENCE (19–20 September 2025)
paragraphs: The Office of Human Resources organised a two-day Professional Development Programme for 22 teachers from Christ School, Hassan, on 19 and 20 September 2025 at the Council Room, Admin Block, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be) University. The programme aimed to enhance teaching competencies, classroom management, student mentoring and leadership skills.

Faculty members conducted sessions on growth-oriented teaching perspectives, innovative classroom management, effective student mentoring, teamwork, institutional collaboration and inspirational leadership. The programme also included an interaction with the Vice Chancellor, campus visits and experience-sharing activities, followed by certificate distribution. The initiative provided teachers with practical insights and effective strategies to strengthen their teaching practices and professional development.

contentBlocks.title: PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME ON INSTITUTIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND UNIVERSITY STATUS (12 November 2025)
paragraphs: The Office of Human Resources facilitated an institutional interaction for 14 officials from Rajagiri School of Engineering and Technology, Ernakulam, on 12 November 2025 at the Council Room, Admin Block, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be) University. The programme aimed to provide insights into the academic, administrative, governance and quality assurance practices involved in attaining university status.

The interaction began with a meeting with the Vice Chancellor, who shared the University's vision, governance structure and academic practices. This was followed by an interactive session with the IQAC team on institutional documentation, academic records management, quality monitoring, accreditation procedures and regulatory compliance. The visiting officials actively participated in the discussions and exchanged institutional experiences. The programme concluded with a guided campus tour, providing an overview of the University's academic and support facilities.

contentBlocks.title: PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME ON INSTITUTIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND UNIVERSITY STATUS (15 November 2025)
paragraphs: The Office of Human Resources organised an institutional interaction for the Principal and 11 faculty members of St. Agnes College (Autonomous), Mangalore, on 15 November 2025 at the Council Room, Admin Block, Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be) University. The programme aimed to familiarise participants with university governance, statutory requirements, examination systems, curriculum frameworks and quality assurance practices.

Dr. Aloysius Edward, Registrar, shared insights into statutory requirements, governance structures and university administration, while Prof. Geo Joy, Controller of Examinations, discussed examination reforms, curriculum design, academic autonomy and examination management systems. The IQAC team highlighted accreditation strategies, institutional quality assurance mechanisms and documentation practices. The visit also included a guided tour of the campus, covering academic blocks, laboratories, the library and student support facilities. The interaction provided the 12 participants with practical insights into university-level academic administration and institutional quality management.

contentBlocks.title: PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME ON FOSTERING INSTITUTIONAL EXCELLENCE (29–30 April 2025)
paragraphs: The Human Resource Development Centre of Kristu Jayanti College (Autonomous) organised a two-day Professional Development Programme titled “Fostering Institutional Excellence” for Carmel Public School, Puliyanmala, Kerala, on 29 and 30 April 2025. The programme featured expert sessions on developing a growth-oriented teaching mindset, enhancing interpersonal effectiveness, classroom management, effective mentoring, collaboration and team synergy, and empowering leadership in schools.

The sessions were facilitated by Dr. Justin Nelson Michael, Dr. Jonas Richard A, Prof. Suku Thomas Samuel, Prof. Soumya Simon, Prof. Sen B Mathews and Rev. Fr. Joshy Mathew. The participants also visited the Kristu Jayanti campus and Christ (Deemed to be University) to gain exposure to institutional infrastructure and academic practices. The programme concluded with an experience-sharing and feedback session, providing participants an opportunity to reflect on their learning and the importance of professional development in fostering institutional excellence.

contentBlocks.title: LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME ON SCHOOL MANAGEMENT AND ENHANCING INSTITUTIONAL EFFECTIVENESS (26–27 May 2025)
paragraphs: The Human Resource Development Centre of Kristu Jayanti College (Autonomous) organised a two-day Leadership Development Programme titled “School Management and Enhancing Institutional Effectiveness” for the Little Flower Mission Education Society on 26 and 27 May 2025. The programme featured sessions on the National Education Policy 2020, NCRF, budgeting, the use of AI tools in education, transformational leadership, interpersonal skills, team building, stakeholder engagement and student-centred learning.

The sessions were facilitated by Fr. Dr. Augustine George, Dr. Aloysius Edward J, Dr. Mary Jacob, Prof. Suku Thomas Samuel and Prof. Sen B Mathews. Participants also visited Kristu Jayanti CMI Public School and Christ (Deemed to be University) to gain insights into institutional practices. The programme concluded with a valedictory session and participant reflections, highlighting the value of the training in enhancing leadership skills and professional competence.

contentBlocks.title: Photo Gallery: Outside-Campus Educational Outreach Activities

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti University has established the Centre for Community Education (CCE) as a flagship initiative dedicated exclusively to community education and outreach. The Centre serves as a platform for extending the University's educational resources, knowledge, expertise and institutional support to the wider community. It focuses on promoting inclusive learning, social awareness, skill development, capacity building and lifelong learning opportunities, particularly among underserved and marginalized sections of society. Through structured educational programs, awareness initiatives, training sessions and community engagement activities, CEE strives to empower individuals, address societal needs and foster meaningful university–community partnerships. The Centre reflects the University's commitment to social responsibility, inclusive education and education for sustainable community development.

During the year 2025, the University continued to strengthen its commitment to extension and community engagement through activities conducted beyond the campus by its various centres and service units. The initiatives connected students with schools, rural and urban communities, care institutions and public spaces. The programmes addressed community needs through awareness, service, education, health and hygiene initiatives, environmental action, rural engagement and civic participation. The activities provided opportunities for students to participate in experiential learning and contribute to social responsibility. These activities will happen regularly with set objectives and achievable outcomes.

contentBlocks.title: Six Thrust Areas of Community Outreach
paragraphs: • Health, hygiene and well-being: Awareness initiatives addressed women’s health and menstrual hygiene, dengue prevention, mental health, nutrition, healthcare, first aid and child safety.

• Education, literacy and life skills: Programmes focused on rural education and literacy, values and life skills, IT education, healthy food awareness, study-material support and learning initiatives.

• Rural development and community engagement: Village-level engagement included rural exposure, village surveys, Shramadhaan, community awareness and initiatives in adopted and neighbouring communities.
• Environmental sustainability and cleanliness: Cleanliness drives and Swachh Bharat-related activities encouraged civic participation and responsibility for cleaner public spaces and communities.

• Social care and community support: Visits and service initiatives at elders’ homes, special schools, migrant settlements and underprivileged communities reflected compassion, inclusion and community support.
• Civic awareness and national service: NCC, KCDC and other initiatives included camps, training, awareness of government schemes, safety, discipline and civic responsibility.

contentBlocks.title: 1. Fostering Women’s Safety and Self Awareness (9 April 2025)

indicators.title: Does your university as a body have a policy that ensures that access to these activities is accessible to all, regardless of ethnicity, religion, disability, immigration status or gender?
indicators.text: 4.3.5 Lifelong learning policy ensuring equitable and non-discriminatory access to all

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti University recognizes lifelong learning as a continuous process through which individuals acquire, update and apply knowledge, skills, values and competencies throughout their lives. Learning may take place through formal education, professional development, short-term courses, online learning, workplace experience, community engagement and independent study.

In a changing social, economic and technological environment, lifelong learning supports personal growth, employability, innovation, civic participation and institutional development. The Institution is committed to creating inclusive, flexible and quality-assured opportunities for students, faculty, staff, alumni and eligible members of the wider community. This policy is guided by equitable access, learner-centred education, continuous professional development, digital inclusion and continuous improvement, and shall be implemented in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements and institutional regulations.

The purpose of this policy is to establish a clear framework for planning, delivering, facilitating, monitoring and improving lifelong learning opportunities beyond the requirements of a single academic programme or qualification.
This policy applies, as relevant to programme eligibility and applicable conditions, to:

contentBlocks.title: Scope of Application
paragraphs: • Current students and research scholars;
• Faculty members and academic leaders;
• Administrative, technical and support staff;
• Alumni and former students;
• Working professionals, adult learners and eligible external participants;
• Community members and partner organisations participating in approved learning initiatives.

Access to particular courses, facilities, platforms or credentials may be subject to admission criteria, registration, fees, licensing, capacity, safety requirements and applicable institutional rules.

contentBlocks.title: Key Policy Objectives
paragraphs: • To provide equitable, inclusive and non-discriminatory access to relevant learning opportunities.
• To promote continuous upskilling, reskilling, interdisciplinary learning and transferable competencies.
• To offer flexible learning formats, including online, blended, face-to-face, evening and weekend delivery wherever feasible.
• To support professional growth of faculty and staff through training, development programmes, peer learning and exposure to emerging practices.
• To enable students and alumni to continue learning, strengthen employability and adapt to changing career and societal needs.
• To encourage entrepreneurship, innovation, research awareness, digital literacy and responsible use of technology.
• To extend learning opportunities to communities through outreach, extension activities and collaboration with external organisations.
• To maintain quality, relevance and accountability through periodic review, learner feedback and outcome assessment.

contentBlocks.title: Principles of Inclusivity & Learner-Centred Education
paragraphs: • Inclusivity and equity: Learning opportunities should be accessible without discrimination on grounds prohibited by applicable law and institutional policy. Reasonable accommodation should be considered for learners with disabilities.
• Learner-centredness: Learning design should respond to learners’ needs, prior knowledge, goals and circumstances and encourage active participation, reflection and independent learning.
• Flexibility: Where feasible, delivery schedules and formats should accommodate working professionals, adult learners and learners with differing responsibilities.
• Quality and relevance: Programmes should have clear learning outcomes, appropriate resources, competent facilitators and suitable methods of assessment or feedback.
• Digital enablement: Digital platforms and resources should be used appropriately, considering accessibility, digital literacy, data protection and alternative support.
• Recognition and progression: Prior learning, work experience and external credentials may be considered where a formal mechanism exists and applicable regulations permit.
• Continuous improvement: Programme design and delivery should be informed by feedback, participation data, outcome evidence and changing learner or industry needs.

contentBlocks.title: 6.1 Lifelong Learning Opportunities
paragraphs: The Institution may develop, offer, host or facilitate lifelong learning opportunities based on identified needs, available expertise and resources. These may include:
• Short-term, certificate, diploma or continuing education programmes, subject to applicable approvals;
• Workshops, seminars, conferences, guest lectures, masterclasses and extension lectures;
• Faculty and staff development programmes, orientation, refresher training and pedagogical development;
• Digital literacy, data literacy, communication, leadership, entrepreneurship and other transferable-skills programmes;
• Industry-oriented training, professional updating, vocational or skill-development initiatives;
• MOOCs and other approved online learning opportunities, including suitable external platforms;
• Research, innovation, interdisciplinary and self-directed learning activities; and
• Community-based learning, public awareness programmes and outreach initiatives.

contentBlocks.title: 6.2 Flexible Modes and Learning Pathways
paragraphs: Programmes may be delivered in face-to-face, online or blended modes, depending on learning outcomes, infrastructure and learner needs. Evening, weekend, vacation-based or modular scheduling may be considered where feasible. The Institution may facilitate re-entry into learning at different stages of life, subject to programme requirements and applicable regulations.

contentBlocks.title: 6.3 Learning Resources and Technology
paragraphs: Eligible learners may be provided access, subject to institutional rules and applicable licences, to library collections, e-resources, learning management systems, recorded lectures, digital repositories, online course catalogues and other learning materials. The Institution should periodically review the relevance and accessibility of these resources and provide guidance or support to learners who need assistance.

contentBlocks.title: 6.4 Faculty and Staff Development
paragraphs: The Institution shall encourage continuous professional development among faculty and staff through relevant training, workshops, conferences, peer learning, research engagement, technology-enabled learning and other approved development activities. Departments and administrative units should identify development needs and, where appropriate, incorporate them into annual or periodic plans.

contentBlocks.title: 6.5 Alumni and Community Engagement
paragraphs: The Institution may engage alumni, employers, professional bodies, industry partners, NGOs, community organisations and subject experts in identifying learning needs and delivering suitable programmes. Access, participation requirements and any applicable charges shall be communicated transparently.

contentBlocks.title: 6.6 Inclusion and Learner Support
paragraphs: Reasonable steps should be taken to reduce avoidable financial, geographical, physical and digital barriers. Depending on resources and programme design, support may include accessible learning materials, counselling, mentoring, orientation, technical assistance, on-campus access to digital resources, flexible participation arrangements or financial support under approved schemes.

contentBlocks.title: 6.7 Recognition of Prior Learning and Credentials
paragraphs: Where permitted by applicable regulations and supported by an approved institutional process, the Institution may consider prior learning, professional experience, non-formal learning or external credentials for recognition, credit, exemption or progression. No credit, equivalence or qualification shall be implied unless formally approved by the competent authority. Certificates and other credentials shall clearly state the nature and requirements of the programme.

contentBlocks.title: 6.8 Quality Assurance
paragraphs: Each programme should, as appropriate to its nature and duration, specify its objectives, intended learning outcomes, target participants, delivery mode, facilitator or organising unit, attendance or participation requirements, assessment or completion criteria, and feedback process. Academic and administrative units shall ensure that programmes follow applicable institutional quality standards, financial procedures and regulatory requirements.

contentBlocks.title: Governance & Stakeholder Roles
paragraphs: • Governing Body/Competent Authority: Approve the policy and major amendments, and provide strategic direction and oversight.
• Institutional Leadership: Promote a culture of lifelong learning, facilitate coordination and consider resource requirements.
• IQAC or designated quality assurance unit: Support quality planning, monitor implementation, review feedback and recommend improvements.

• Designated Lifelong Learning/Continuing Education Coordinator or equivalent: Coordinate programme planning, maintain consolidated records, facilitate communication and prepare periodic implementation reports.
• Deans, Heads of Departments and Unit Heads: Identify learning needs, propose relevant programmes, nominate resource persons and support delivery and review.
• Faculty members and trainers: Design or deliver appropriate learning content, guide participants and maintain suitable academic and professional standards.
• Library, IT and support units: Facilitate access to approved learning resources, platforms, technical support and accessible facilities within their respective mandates.
• Learners and participants: Participate responsibly, comply with programme requirements and codes of conduct, respect intellectual property and provide constructive feedback.

contentBlocks.text: The designated unit or responsible departments should identify learning needs through stakeholder consultation, feedback, academic review, professional trends and community engagement. A periodic programme calendar may be prepared, indicating the programme title, target group, mode, schedule, responsible unit and registration process. Programme information, eligibility, fees (if any), learning outcomes and completion requirements should be communicated through official institutional channels. The Institution may collaborate with external institutions, industry, professional bodies, government agencies and community organisations, subject to appropriate approvals and agreements. Participation and completion records should be maintained in accordance with institutional record-management and data-protection requirements.

Lifelong learning initiatives shall be monitored periodically to assess reach, quality, relevance and outcomes. Evaluation may include: number and type of programmes conducted and learner groups reached; participation, attendance, completion and repeat-participation data, as appropriate; learner satisfaction and feedback from facilitators, employers or community partners; evidence of learning, such as assessment results, demonstrations, completed projects or participant reflections, where suitable; accessibility and inclusion concerns, including barriers reported by learners; and recommendations, corrective actions and improvements made for subsequent offerings. The responsible unit shall consolidate relevant information and submit periodic reports to the designated institutional authority or quality assurance body, as prescribed by institutional procedures. Indicators should be interpreted in context and should not substitute for qualitative evaluation.

Implementation shall be supported through approved institutional budgets, departmental resources, grants, collaboration or programme fees, where applicable. All expenditure, fee collection, concessions and financial assistance shall follow the Institution’s approved financial policies and procedures. Resource commitments shall be subject to availability and competent-authority approval.

All programmes and participants shall comply with applicable laws, regulatory requirements and institutional policies relating to academic integrity, conduct, health and safety, intellectual property, use of digital platforms, confidentiality and data protection. Misrepresentation of qualifications, misuse of institutional resources or breach of programme conditions may result in action under applicable institutional rules.

This policy shall be reviewed at least once every three years, or earlier where required by changes in applicable regulations, institutional priorities, technology, learner needs or quality assurance findings. The designated policy owner shall coordinate the review and submit proposed amendments to the competent authority for approval.
